mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in FEDFUNDS above 5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses during a recession.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 of more than 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly below zero during periods of confirmed GDP contraction.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in UNRATE above 4% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive during periods of high unemployment or during periods of strong productivity growth.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months indicates weakening industrial production, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month MA for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during confirmed industrial production contractions.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in both GDPC1 and HOUST signals a broad-based deterioration in demand, which depresses earnings and equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of such co-declining episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in CPIAUCSL above 4% while FEDFUNDS remains below 2% for three months signals an inflation surprise with accommodative policy, which erodes real purchasing power and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 4% and FEDFUNDS < 2% for three months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in PAYEMS above 0.5% for three consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 0.5% monthly growth for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods of strong payroll growth.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in RSAFS above its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals rising household savings, which often coincides with precautionary behavior and weaker consumption, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-month MA for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when household savings accelerate persistently.
